_about: Monta T-bar (surface lift, modern), rebuilt to the owner's reference installation: the drive at the bottom (D1) and the return at the top, a tower kit (heads, 1 m mast sections, base; every mast leaning across the line, D11), the carriers (recoil box on its grip, T bar and J bar) and the operator hut. Millimetres in the lift frame: origin on the bullwheel's axle (a terminal) or the mast top (a head) or at grade (a base, mast section, hut), u toward the line (uphill on a tower), v right, w up. The loaded (uphill) rope is on the right going up: v+ at the bottom terminal, v- at the top one.

train._about: A sheave train on one rope: sheaves in pairs on rockers with a cheek plate each side, the rockers' pins on a pentagonal equaliser inboard of them, the equaliser on the end pin through the crossarm's end plate. Support trains stand on the pin with the rope on top; hold-down trains hang inverted from the same pin. The axles sit on an arc of radius arcR about the rope's bend. Offsets in v run inboard from the sheave's hub: cheek gap, cheek, equaliser gap, equaliser, end gap, end plate.

tower._lean: D11/Q1: every mast leans this many degrees across the line toward the loaded track; ropes level, the foundation off to the return side

base._stub: the mast's first stretch is part of the base, wrapped in the red tower pad (D5); mast_foot at its top along the leaned axis

head._catcher: black tube out from each end of each train, inside the carrier hanger's D (out of v, below the rope), so a swinging hanger can't reach the sheaves; flare: [where the tip bends, out, down]

drive._about: The bottom station (D1): one box column on a concrete block, its lower part the cabinet; a head frame of two girders along the line; the bullwheel hung under a railed deck behind the column with the machinery house on it; a railed walkway toward the line over two hold-down trains (8 sheaves on the leaving loaded rope, v+, 4 on the arriving one); the loading hoop on an outboard bracket at the girders' end; a ladder between the ropes. Rope at 3.4 m (D8).
drive._hoop: the loading hoop round the retracted bar's stem (below the recoil box, above the T), at the girders' end; its bracket runs out past the carriers' hangers (out) and down

return._about: The top station: one box column leaning back toward the wheel and a plumb strut on a flat pad, carrying the same girders; the bullwheel cantilevered behind on its shaft from a bearing housing (the tensioning hidden inside, D2); 8-sheave hold-down trains on both ropes toward the line; a railed walkway, a ladder up the column's line face, the A-frame for the wire (D9). Rope at 4.5 m (Q4).

hut._about: The operator hut (D9, Q3): red walls on skids, a mono-pitch white roof falling toward +u, the door and a window on the -u face, a window each side.

carrier._about: Carriers: a small dark clamp grip on the rope's outboard side; from it one hanger tube sweeps outboard and down in a half ellipse (the rope its straight side, a D) and comes back in to the recoil box, a pale rounded housing that hangs on a pin through its upper part, swinging fore and aft, nearly back under the rope; the cord leaves a collar at its bottom. The bar: a yellow stem with a plain socket at its top where the cord ends, and one continuous black padded crossbar (T) or a yellow J curve. Grip origin on the rope; u the way the carrier travels, +v outboard, w up. The bars' origin at their eye (the socket's top).

grip._grip: the clamp outboard of the sheaves' faces (vIn past the sheave's half width), its thin jaw reaching in to the rope inside the liners' clearance, so it passes support and hold-down sheaves and the bullwheel's groove (C12)
